I would **escalate the box urgently, but I would not change its storage date or remove it from the destruction batch without an authorised instruction**.

The letters and photographs are known to be irreplaceable, so I would immediately alert the manager and the relevant operations contact, state that destruction is scheduled today and that Claire’s authorised collection is booked for Wednesday, and ask whether an approved emergency hold or written extension can be registered before 13:30. I would not treat the pending request, the collection booking, or Claire’s authority as approval to change the storage date. Nor would I quietly move the box to reserve: that would be an unauthorised extension and would create the work order and charge.

On the facts given, no approver can provide permission before the deadline, and the manager has explicitly directed release of the full batch. **Unless a valid authorised instruction arrives in time, I would release the full manifest**, including this box, and document the request and escalation accurately. That is a distressing outcome, but holding the whole manifest or making an unapproved exception would also breach the stated process; a later approval cannot cover an earlier date change.

Afterward, I would raise the case for review so the centre can address how urgent, irreversible cases are handled when no approver is available.
